title: AtlasHealth — Contract stretch + region onramp review
summary: Quarterly renewal/expansion check-in focused on adding EU region, testing private VPC path, and bumping Dedicated capacity by 30%. Customer raised latency budget vs cost concerns and requested a short benchmarking pilot and updated pricing. Action items surfaced around security docs, billing amendment, and an on-prem checklist.
next_steps: Maya to send updated 12-month pricing and 30% uplift amendment by 2028-11-13
Diego to schedule a 2-week benchmarking pilot (EU region) and provide test config by 2028-11-16
Connor to share onboarding runbook + VPC checklist link (docs.redwood.io/vpc-onboard) by 2028-11-12
Customer to confirm internal stakeholders and sign-off timeline by 2028-11-20
action_items: Maya - Prepare amended SOW and pricing table, due 2028-11-13
Diego - Build pilot workload YAML and run initial latency/cost runs in eu-west, due 2028-11-16
Connor - Share private deployment checklist + KMS integration guide, due 2028-11-12
Rachel - Confirm security reviewer and preferred audit window, due 2028-11-20
questions: Can Redwood Dedicated hit 95th perc p99 < 90ms for our 1-2k token prompts?
If we start with hosted EU and then transition to VPC, what is the rollback policy?
How do you handle KMS/HSM key rotation in Private deployments?
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-11-09 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Connor (CSM), Rachel Morgan (AtlasHealth), Samir Khan (Atlas CTO), Olivia Park (Platform), Evan Blake (Procurement)

Auto summary (auto): Customer is evaluating a 12-month extension with a 30% capacity uplift and wants to enable an EU region immediately; exploring private VPC pilot in Q1 2029. Security docs (SOC2, SAML, KMS/HSM) requested. Benchmark pilot to validate latency/cost tradeoffs.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining. quick check, i think we have the usual suspects — rachel, samir, olivia, evan — can you hear me okay?
[00:06] Rachel: yes, loud and clear. morning for some of us — afternoon — yeah all good.
[00:12] Maya: awesome. objective today is to align on the renewal timeline, the proposed 30% dedicated bump, and the EU onramp, plus any blockers for a private/VPC pilot.
[00:20] Samir: perfect. we got your note, and procurement's looped in — evan will be the sign-off owner. main thing from our side is latency — our clinicians demand snappy responses — but budget is tight so want to see the numbers.
[00:32] Diego: totally, so high level — Dedicated can give you predictable throughput; the p99 will depend on model shape and prompt length — from what we saw in the eval you sent, most requests average ~900 tokens with spikes to 2k. our routing + prefix KV cash (sic) helps, but we should run a short pilot to quantify.
[00:50] Olivia: small note — we prefer to start in hosted EU and then flip to VPC if we like it. migrating shouldn't be a huge deal but need to understand egress/billing and keys.
[01:03] Connor: i'll drop the VPC checklist after the call — it's the usual: network ranges, peering, KMS info, audit log endpoints.
[01:10] Rachel: on security — SOC two is fine; can you share the SOC 2 plus ISO pack? also want SSO via SAML and RBAC mapping.
[01:21] Maya: yes we'll share our security one-pager and the full SOC2 report. we also have the KMS integration guide — diego will paste that link.

[01:35] Speaker 6: sorry just joined, quick question — what's the fallback if your eu region is saturated?
[01:40] Diego: good one — we have smart routing policies. default is to failover to nearby region (eu-west -> us-west fallback only if policy allows) or to a cheaper/compatible model variant; we can set strict latency-first routing for production so requests don't go cross-continent.
[01:56] Samir: ok, cost. how does dedicated pricing vs hosted differ for committed blocks?
[02:02] Maya: dedicated is a reservation-style commit — predictable monthly fee with a token-based add-on if you burst. hosted is pay-as-you-go. with a 12-month commit we can structure a tiered discount and capacity burst buffer. we'll propose specifics in the amendment.

[02:20] Rachel: timeline — we want EU region live by end of November if possible, or early December latest. is that realistic?
[02:28] Diego: for hosted EU yes, it's almost a flipping of a flag if capacity is available; for VPC/private onboarding that'll be a Q1 2029 activity — involves network provisioning and audit window.
[02:38] Olivia: can we do quick sanity benchmarks in eu-west this week? even 48 hours would help.
[02:44] Diego: yes, we can run a 2-week bench pilot with your traffic sample. initial smoke runs possible within 48 hours — need a test API key and the prompt set.
[02:53] Olivia: we'll prepare the set.

[03:00] Evan: proc question — if we extend the contract and then want to reduce capacity after 6 months, is that allowed?
[03:06] Maya: depends on the term. typically commits are fixed for the period but we can include a quarterly re-eval clause or a staged uplift with a partial break clause — i'll propose language.
[03:15] Samir: any hidden egress charges when moving data between regions or into our VPC?
[03:21] Diego: egress is cloud provider cost; for hosted EU to your VPC there is data transfer — we'll surface estimates and options to minimize egress (edge caching, prefix caching).

[03:35] Rachel: security — how do you do key rotation in Private? our compliance team insists on HSM-backed rotation quarterly.
[03:43] Diego: private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM; rotations are supported, and we record key metadata in audit logs. small caveat — rotations require a short rekey window for any long-lived KV cache tokens. we'll put that in the runbook.
[03:58] Speaker 6: there's some noise on the transcript — transcripts sometime say KV "cash".
[04:03] Maya: yeah fireflies loves that one.

[04:10] Maya: let's walk the proposed pilot plan: 1) Redwood provisions a hosted EU sandbox with a Dedicated-like profile, 2) Atlas pushes representative traffic for 2 weeks, 3) Redwood runs latency/cost breakdown and knob tuning (batching, quant profiles), 4) decide on VPC pilot. agreed?
[04:26] Rachel: agreed. what telemetry do you need? traces, per-token breakdown?
[04:30] Diego: traces + per-token cost, token-level latency histograms, and trace ids so we can map to your backend. also sequence length distribution.

[04:40] Olivia: regarding model variants — if we quantize a variant to reduce cost, what's the risk to hallucination/quality?
[04:47] Diego: depends on the model and quant format; for many of the Llama-family variants the difference is minor for classification but can impact generation in edge cases. Redwood Optimize will run a quality regression against your eval set and flag regressions.

[04:58] Evan: procurement — can you provide a redlineable amendment asap?
[05:03] Maya: yes, we'll do a draft SOW + amendment with the 30% uplift and a staged payout; target to get that by next tues (2028-11-13).

[05:12] Samir: on costs — can we get a blended unit price if we commit 12 months + an EU region?
[05:18] Maya: yes, that's standard — blended pricing across regions with a small premium for private. i'll include two options: hosted-eu-first and dedicated-reserved-first.

[05:28] Diego: operational note — if you want strict p99 < 90ms we may need to increase instance density and reduce batching; that increases per-token cost. we can show the tradeoff in the bench.

[05:40] Rachel: ok, decision points then: 1) do the 2-week bench in EU (yes), 2) sign 12-month with 30% uplift (tentative until bench results), 3) plan VPC pilot for Q1.
[05:52] Maya: great. i'll recap after the call.

[05:58] Connor: action — i'll send runbook and onboarding link now; diego will follow up with pilot questions.
[06:05] Diego: quick note, please include sample worst-case prompts so we can hit tail latency scenarios.
[06:10] Olivia: will do.

[06:15] Maya: any final blockers?
[06:18] Samir: none for now, just need the amendment and bench results.
[06:22] Rachel: same. also could you include the SLA response windows and escalation contacts?
[06:27] Maya: yes, that goes in the SOW.

[06:35] Maya: thanks everyone — we'll send the docs and schedule follow-ups.
[06:40] Evan: thanks.
[06:42] Rachel: thanks all.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription quality: medium — occasional word swaps (e.g., KV cash), speaker attribution minor errors. Links mentioned: docs.redwood.io/vpc-onboard (runbook), internal bench sheet (link to be shared by diego).
file_notes: Recorded in UTC. AE-led with SE and CSM present. Clear renewal expansion theme; unique phrasing in title to avoid duplication with other check-ins. Contains explicit next steps and action items as requested by procurement and security teams.
